doc.title: Bernie Kirsh interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 27, 2022

title: Chick's Scientology and his music
summary: Rowe asks about Scientology's role in Chick's music; Kirsh says the music comes from his soul.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Did Chick’s devotion to Scientology come to work with him?
In what respect do you mean?
Did you get the feeling that decisions he made were based on his belief in Scientology?

Well I can’t imagine that the things that people know to be true for themselves wouldn’t be expressed by them. I think that’s probably true for anything. If you have a certain idea of how things are in the world and how you treat others then you would treat them that way and so forth. Is that what you mean? That sort of thing?
I guess so. It was not a well formed question but I was sort of curious about what role it played in his musical life?

It’s hard for me to say. I mean because when you’re hearing music coming you’re hearing the whole thing you know? I can’t imagine that there wasn’t some influence in his understanding of the world for sure, but the music comes from his soul. You know it doesn’t come from — there’s not something else that is his music. You know it’s something that he’s decided he wanted to make. How he lives his life and how he sees the world that may be influenced by philosophy and so forth. But the creative process is a process that’s the most personal thing you can do. It’s the nearest thing to not being in this world that you can do. I mean I don’t know, I mean I don’t know if you’ve had the experience. I have, where the world goes away and you’re just creating. So — and I think that’s what occurs because it’s coming from that place and that place is not in this world.
